nodes.label: main()
nodes.desc: Entry point: parses argv, loads config (conf.c), opens the database with db__open, sets up listeners and bridges, then enters mosquitto_main_loop.

nodes.label: mosquitto_main_loop()
nodes.desc: Single-threaded broker loop: retain expiry, plugin message queue, keepalive check, bridge check, plugin tick events, session expiry, will delay, then mux__handle() and the persistence autosave.

nodes.label: mux__handle()
nodes.desc: Compile-time vtable selecting epoll (Linux), kqueue (BSD/macOS) or poll as the readiness engine; everything else calls the neutral mux__* API.

nodes.label: mux_epoll__handle()
nodes.desc: epoll_wait with a computed timeout (db.next_event_ms); accepts new clients on listener sockets and calls packet__read()/packet__write() on ready clients.

nodes.label: net__socket_accept()
nodes.desc: accept() on a listener, allocates the per-client context (context__init) and registers the fd with the mux so its traffic joins the same readiness loop.

nodes.label: keepalive__check()
nodes.desc: Ticks every loop iteration; disconnects clients that missed their keepalive window using a hashed time-bucket structure.

nodes.label: session_expiry__check()
nodes.desc: MQTT 5 session expiry: expired offline sessions are cleaned up by the loop instead of by a separate thread.

nodes.label: handle__packet()
nodes.desc: Broker-side dispatch on the fixed-header control byte, bumping mosq_counter_* $SYS metrics for every received packet type.

nodes.label: handle__connect()
nodes.desc: CONNECT: validates client id and protocol level, restores or creates the session, registers the will, then runs basic auth before CONNACK.

nodes.label: handle__publish()
nodes.desc: PUBLISH: parses topic, payload and MQTT 5 properties (topic alias expansion, message expiry interval), validates QoS, then hands the message to the store.

nodes.label: handle__accepted_publish()
nodes.desc: Once the message is stored, fan-out happens per QoS level: QoS 0/1 call sub__messages_queue() immediately, and PUBACK/PUBREC answers are sent back to the publisher.

nodes.label: handle__subscribe()
nodes.desc: SUBSCRIBE: validates each filter against ACLs, inserts subleafs, handles no-local and retain-as-published options, replays retained messages, sends SUBACK.

nodes.label: handle__auth()
nodes.desc: MQTT 5 enhanced authentication: AUTH packets flow to the registered extended-auth plugin until CONNACK completes.

nodes.label: sub__add()
nodes.desc: Inserts a subscription leaf into the hashed topic tree, creating intermediate mosquitto__subhier nodes per topic level as needed.

nodes.label: sub__messages_queue()
nodes.desc: Walks the tree level by level, matching # and + wildcards, collecting overlapping subscriptions and merging subscription identifiers before delivery.

nodes.label: subs__process()
nodes.desc: For every matching subleaf, applies retain-as-published/no-local semantics and queues the message into the subscriber's outgoing QoS state via subs__send().

nodes.label: subs__shared_process()
nodes.desc: MQTT 5 shared subscriptions ($share/group/topic): round-robins one message to one member of the group instead of broadcasting.

nodes.label: retain__store()
nodes.desc: Replaces the stored message in the mosquitto__retainhier branch (or deletes it on zero-length retained payload); expiry is checked by the main loop.

nodes.label: retain__queue()
nodes.desc: On SUBSCRIBE, walks the retain tree with retain__search() and sends every retained message matching the new filter.

nodes.label: struct mosquitto__base_msg
nodes.desc: The ref-counted stored message: one allocation shared by all subscribers, with dest_ids, ref_count and per-client mosquitto__client_msg records tracking QoS delivery state.

nodes.label: db__message_store()
nodes.desc: Adds the base_msg to the global store hash and assigns a store id; db__msg_store_ref_inc() tracks each subscriber reference.

nodes.label: db__message_insert_outgoing()
nodes.desc: Attaches a client_msg to the receiving session, respecting inflight quota, then schedules the PUBLISH write via the mux.

nodes.label: db__message_insert_incoming()
nodes.desc: Incoming QoS 2 bookkeeping: stores the message on behalf of the publisher until PUBREL completes the handshake.

nodes.label: persist__backup()
nodes.desc: Writes the persistence DB (v5 format in persist_write_v5.c): clients, subscriptions, retained messages, in-flight messages. Triggered by autosave_interval in the main loop.

nodes.label: persist__restore()
nodes.desc: At startup, replays the DB (v5 and legacy v234 readers) so sessions, subscriptions and queued QoS messages survive broker restarts.

nodes.label: mosquitto_callback_register()
nodes.desc: Every security mechanism registers event callbacks here: MOSQ_EVT_BASIC_AUTH, MOSQ_EVT_EXTENDED_AUTH, MOSQ_EVT_ACL_CHECK, MOSQ_EVT_MESSAGE, MOSQ_EVT_TICK.

nodes.label: broker_password_file__init()
nodes.desc: The built-in password file is itself just a plugin: parses passwd entries then registers password_file__check as a MOSQ_EVT_BASIC_AUTH callback.

nodes.label: mosquitto_plugin_init()
nodes.desc: The dynamic-security plugin loads its JSON config and registers auth, ACL and control-callback events so clients/groups/roles can be managed at runtime.

nodes.label: dynsec__handle_command()
nodes.desc: Handles $CONTROL/dynamic-security/v1 commands (createClient, createRole...) that arrive via the broker's control topic from mosquitto_ctrl.

nodes.label: mosquitto_broker_publish()
nodes.desc: Plugin API for injecting messages into the broker (e.g. dynsec replies); a parallel BROKER_EXPORT surface lets plugins inspect and kick clients.

nodes.label: mosquitto_new()
nodes.desc: Client library entry: allocates a struct mosquitto instance; the same lib/ sources are compiled into the broker for packet parsing, so both sides share wire-format code.

nodes.label: mosquitto_loop()
nodes.desc: Client-side event loop: select()/pselect() on the socket plus a sockpair to wake the thread, then mosquitto_loop_read/write/misc.

nodes.label: handle__packet()
nodes.desc: Client-side dispatch mirrors the broker: PINGRESP, PUBACK, PUBLISH (from broker), CONNACK... plus MQTT 5 DISCONNECT with precise reason codes on protocol errors.

nodes.label: packet__read()
nodes.desc: Shared wire-format reader: remaining-length varint parsing and packet assembly, used by both the broker (via the mux) and the client (via mosquitto_loop).
